definition: Recapitulate means to summarize and restate the main points.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word recapitulate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know recapitulate should be able to work it out from your sentence.

Touch on is a much slighter pass than recapitulate — a speaker names a topic in a phrase and moves along, stating nothing of substance about it.
Sum up goes further than touch on — the gist gets stated squarely — but it stops short of recapitulate, which walks back through the points in order and restates each one.

Restate means to say a point again, usually in fresh words, to make it clearer or firmer — one point at a time, with no promise of order or coverage. Recapitulate is systematic where restate is piecemeal: it walks back through all the main points, in order, so the whole holds together.

Go over is the casual phrase for revisiting material — informally, in any order, at whatever length the moment allows. Recapitulate is its formal cousin, at home in lectures, briefings, and closing arguments, and it promises an ordered, point-by-point return through everything that matters.
